To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) action detection can be learned in an end-to-end fashion by observing only a small fraction of video frames; (2) the process of action detection can be formulated as a sequential decision making process, and can be learned using reinforcement learning techniques; and (3) our method is able to learn a policy that is able to generalize to videos that are unseen during training, which is a desirable property of action detection models

(1) a recurrent agent that observes video frame glimpses can learn to accurately detect action boundaries in videos; (2) this agent can learn to detect actions with very few glimpses; and (3) our approach outperforms the state of the art in action detection.

1) we present the first fully end-to-end model for action detection in video, and 2) we show that this approach achieves state-of-the art performance on two large scale action detection datasets, while only observing 2% of the video frames
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can we learn to detect actions in videos by only observing a few frames at a time? How can we do so in an end-to-end fashion? What are the advantages of such an approach?
the problem of action detection in videos.

the following question: can we train a model to detect actions in a video by only showing it glimpses of the video? Our answer is that we can, and that we can do so better than previous approaches that have access to the full video.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our model achieves state-of-art action detection performance while observing only a small fraction (2% and less) of the frames in the video.
the proposed model is able to learn the action detection task end-to-end, and it is able to achieve state-of-the-art performance while using very few glimpses of the video.
the proposed method is able to learn to detect actions in videos by observing only a fraction of the frames, which can be seen as a form of active perception.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have introduced a new approach for action detection that learns to observe the video and predict action instances in an end-to-end fashion.
we introduce an end-to-end trainable model for action detection that can observe only a few glimpses of a video and still perform well.
our model can learn to detect actions in video from very little data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the process by which humans perform action detection is fundamentally different from the way it is modeled by existing methods.
we can achieve strong results on the action detection task without relying on hand-crafted features or complex temporal models.
it is possible to learn an action detector that is able to observe only glimpses of a video and still achieve state-of-the-art performance.
